Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No state transit- or bus-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault statutes cover causing or attempting physical injury, serious physical injury, or injury with a deadly weapon/dangerous instrument.
Punishment / grading: First degree Class B felony; second degree Class C felony; third degree Class A misdemeanor.
Notes: No separate public-transit-driver category found in current state assault code.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: State law: no state transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located. Local example: Anchorage protects public transit workers.
Statute number(s): State: AS 11.41.200-11.41.230; Anchorage Municipal Code sections 8.05.015, 8.10.010, 11.70.030
Covered worker/setting: Public transit worker under Anchorage ordinance; general victims under Alaska state assault statutes
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Anchorage assault is distinct when committed against a public transit worker and the offender knows or reasonably should know the worker is engaged in official duties.
Felony or misdemeanor: State: depends on degree; Anchorage: Class A misdemeanor
Punishment / grading: Anchorage class A misdemeanor; transit-worker status may be an aggravating factor at sentencing; conviction for assaulting a public transit worker carries an automatic 1-year transit-system ban.
Notes: Local ordinances were not exhaustively surveyed; Anchorage is included because it directly surfaced and is transit-specific.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault on a public transit employee can be aggravated assault.
Statute number(s): A.R.S. section 13-1204(A)(8)(k), as amended by 2025 Ariz. Sess. Laws ch. 172
Covered worker/setting: Public transit employee performing duties on or off a bus, van, or shuttle while transferring community members
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Aggravated assault includes an assault where the victim is a public transit employee performing duties on/off a vehicle while engaged in transferring community members to and from destinations in a bus, van, or shuttle.
Punishment / grading: Arizona Class 6 felony; for first felony under general sentencing, presumptive 1 year, range commonly 4 months to 2 years, subject to Arizona sentencing rules.
Notes: Current as enacted in 2025 and in force by research date.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No assault-specific transit-driver enhancement located; separate bus-conduct offenses exist.
Statute number(s): Ark. Code sections 5-13-201 to 5-13-205; section 5-60-112; section 5-39-214
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims; bus passengers/driver orders; school buses
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault applies. Bus misconduct includes failure to obey a reasonable request or order of a bus driver or authorized company representative; unauthorized entry of a school bus is separately prohibited.
Felony or misdemeanor: General assault: depends; bus misconduct generally misdemeanor
Punishment / grading: Assault degrees vary; first-degree assault is Class A misdemeanor; bus misconduct penalties are separate and not a violence enhancement.
Distinct from violence in general?: Limited bus-conduct distinction; not a violence-against-driver enhancement
Notes: No public-transit-driver assault felony/misdemeanor enhancement located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Separate assault/battery provisions for public transportation settings and transportation personnel/passengers.
Covered worker/setting: Public transportation provider property/vehicle; operators, drivers, passengers, station/ticket agents, public transportation providers, employees/contractors
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 241.3 covers assault against any person on public transportation provider property or vehicle. section 243.3 covers battery against operators, drivers, passengers, agents, providers, employees, or contractors when duty/status elements are met. section 245.2 covers assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily injury against transportation operators/drivers/passengers/agents.
Punishment / grading: section 241.3: up to 1 year jail/$2,000. section 243.3: up to 1 year/$10,000; if injury requiring medical treatment, wobbler up to 3 years. section 245.2: state prison 3, 4, or 5 years.
Notes: California also has related robbery/murder provisions for transportation workers/passengers, but this table focuses on assault/battery violence.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes, but framed as harassment/interference with a transit worker, not a general assault enhancement.
Covered worker/setting: Transit worker; RTD employees/agents
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Criminal harassment includes wrongfully interfering with a transit worker performing a lawful duty. RTD law separately prohibits wrongfully interfering with a district officer, agent, or employee.
Felony or misdemeanor: Class 1 misdemeanor for transit-worker harassment; Class 2 misdemeanor for RTD interference
Punishment / grading: CO Class 1 misdemeanor generally up to 364 days jail/$1,000; Class 2 misdemeanor generally up to 120 days/$750.
Notes: 2025 law; avoid treating it as an assault reclassification.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault of public transit personnel and aggravated assault of a public transit employee are separate felonies.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit personnel and public transit employees
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 53a-167c covers assaulting public transit personnel with intent to prevent duties, including injury, objects, chemical agents, noxious substances, or bodily fluids. section 53a-167e covers aggravated assault of a public transit employee with knife/box-cutter/firearm use, display, threat, or possession.
Punishment / grading: Class C felony: 1 to 10 years; section 53a-167e includes fine up to $20,000.
Notes: Definitions include fixed-route bus/ferry and rail-related workers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Public transit operators are protected in assault in the second and first degree.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit operator acting in lawful performance of duty
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Second-degree assault includes intentionally causing physical injury to a public transit operator acting in lawful duty. First-degree assault includes intentionally causing serious physical injury to a public transit operator acting in lawful duty.
Felony or misdemeanor: Class D felony for section 612 transit-operator physical injury; Class B felony for section 613 serious physical injury
Punishment / grading: Class D felony up to 8 years; Class B felony 2 to 25 years.
Notes: section 612 title says class C or D felony; the transit-operator injury paragraph is treated as Class D unless another paragraph applies.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Enhanced penalties for crimes of violence against transit operators and Metrorail station employees/managers/passengers.
Statute number(s): D.C. Code section 22-3751.01; notice requirement section 35-261
Covered worker/setting: Transit operators, Metrorail station managers/employees, mass-transit-vehicle passengers
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Any person who commits a crime of violence against a transit operator operating a mass transit vehicle in D.C., or against on-duty Metrorail station personnel/passengers, may receive enhanced punishment.
Punishment / grading: Up to 1.5 times the otherwise-authorized maximum imprisonment and fine.
Notes: Works as an enhancement, not a standalone assault degree.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault/battery against public transit employees or agents is reclassified upward.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit employees or agents, including bus operators, train operators, revenue collectors, security, maintenance, field supervisors
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Knowingly committing assault, battery, aggravated assault, or aggravated battery upon listed personnel, including public transit employees/agents, while they are engaged in lawful duties triggers reclassification.
Punishment / grading: Assault: 2nd-degree misdemeanor to 1st-degree misdemeanor. Battery: 1st-degree misdemeanor to 3rd-degree felony. Aggravated assault: 3rd-degree felony to 2nd-degree felony. Aggravated battery: 2nd-degree felony to 1st-degree felony.
Notes: General Florida maximums: 1st-degree misdemeanor up to 1 year/$1,000; 3rd-degree felony up to 5 years/$5,000; 2nd-degree felony up to 15 years/$10,000; 1st-degree felony up to 30 years/$10,000.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes, but mainly based on the public transit vehicle/station setting rather than driver status.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit vehicle or station; any victim in that setting
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Simple assault, simple battery, battery, aggravated assault, and aggravated battery committed in a public transit vehicle or station receive specified enhanced grading/punishment.
Punishment / grading: Simple assault/battery/battery in transit setting are misdemeanors of a high and aggravated nature; aggravated assault in transit setting 3 to 20 years; aggravated battery in transit setting 5 to 20 years.
Distinct from violence in general?: Yes, for transit setting; not only bus drivers
Notes: Public-transit setting distinction can protect drivers but is not limited to drivers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Interference with a public transit operator is a separate felony.
Covered worker/setting: Operator of a public transit vehicle
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Interference occurs when a person intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causes bodily injury to the operator, or recklessly creates a substantial risk of bodily injury to the operator, while the operator is operating or otherwise in control of a public transit vehicle.
Punishment / grading: Class C felony: up to 5 years imprisonment; fine generally up to $10,000.
Notes: Hawaii frames the offense as interference with the operator rather than ordinary assault.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Limited school-bus-specific protection; no public-transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Statute number(s): Idaho Code section 18-1522; general assault/battery sections 18-901, 18-903, 18-905
Covered worker/setting: School bus driver; general assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Interfering with or obstructing the driver of a school bus, or entering a school bus with intent to commit a crime or disrupt/impede operation, is prohibited.
Felony or misdemeanor: Misdemeanor for school-bus interference; general assault/battery varies
Punishment / grading: Misdemeanor punishment generally up to 6 months/$1,000 unless a specific statute applies; aggravated battery may be felony.
Notes: No current state public-transit operator assault enhancement located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Aggravated assault/battery provisions cover transportation-system personnel and passengers.
Covered worker/setting: Driver, operator, employee, or passenger of a transportation facility or system engaged in duties or using the system
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Aggravated assault and aggravated battery include offenses against drivers, operators, employees, or passengers of a transportation facility/system. Posting law states assault against a transit employee is Class A misdemeanor and physical harm is Class 3 felony.
Punishment / grading: Aggravated assault commonly Class A misdemeanor; some weapon/firearm forms are felonies. Aggravated battery against covered transportation personnel/passengers generally Class 3 felony.
Notes: Illinois has both criminal provisions and transit notice/signage requirements.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault/battery victims; school employees may be separately protected if status elements apply
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General battery statute grades injury/contact offenses; no current public-transit-driver category located.
Felony or misdemeanor: Misdemeanor or felony depending injury/victim status
Punishment / grading: Basic battery is Class B misdemeanor; grading rises for injury, serious injury, deadly weapon, and listed protected classes.
Notes: School bus drivers may be covered in some school-employee scenarios, but no transit-operator-specific provision located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault covers acts intended to cause pain/injury, insulting or offensive contact, or placing another in fear of immediate physical contact.
Felony or misdemeanor: Misdemeanor or felony depending assault type/injury
Punishment / grading: Assault penalties range from simple misdemeanor to aggravated misdemeanor or Class D felony depending injury, weapon, and intent.
Notes: No separate public-transit or bus-driver assault statute located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault/battery victims; school employees may be protected in limited circumstances
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault/battery statutes apply; school-employee status can affect battery grading if statutory elements are met, but no public-transit-driver category was located.
Punishment / grading: Assault/battery grading varies from misdemeanor to felony depending injury, weapon, and protected victim category.
Notes: No current state public-transit operator assault enhancement located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Limited school-bus-specific protection; no public-transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: School bus driver acting in course of duty; general assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault in the third degree includes intentionally causing or attempting to cause physical injury to a school bus driver while the driver is acting in the course of official duties.
Punishment / grading: Class D felony: 1 to 5 years.
Notes: No separate public-transit bus-operator statute located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Battery of a bus operator or train operator is a separate offense.
Covered worker/setting: Bus operator or train operator while operating a bus/train
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Statute covers battery committed without consent when the offender has reasonable grounds to believe the victim is a bus operator or train operator operating a bus or train.
Felony or misdemeanor: Misdemeanor, with mandatory minimum jail component
Punishment / grading: Imprisonment 72 hours to 1 year, with or without hard labor, and/or fine up to $1,000; at least 72 hours without benefit of probation, parole, or suspension of sentence.
Notes: Current Louisiana statute was amended after the older 2012 chart; use current penalty language.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault statutes cover bodily injury, offensive physical contact, serious bodily injury, or dangerous weapon scenarios.
Punishment / grading: Assault is generally Class D; elevated assault is Class C; aggravated assault is Class B.
Notes: No current state transit-operator assault enhancement located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes for interference and transit bans after assault allegations; no assault-degree reclassification located.
Covered worker/setting: Transit vehicle operator; station agent, conductor, or station attendant; alleged assault on public transit operator or passenger
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 7-705(f) makes it unlawful to obstruct, hinder, or interfere with the operation or operator of a transit vehicle/railroad passenger car or listed station/rail personnel. section 7-705.1 permits prohibiting a person alleged to have committed assault or another intentional bodily-injury act against a public transit operator or passenger from using state transit or entering stations.
Punishment / grading: Misdemeanor under section 7-705(f): fine up to $1,000 and imprisonment up to 1 year, or both.
Distinct from violence in general?: Yes for interference/transit exclusion, not assault grading
Notes: Maryland's new section 7-705.1 is not a criminal penalty enhancement; it creates a transit-use/station-ban process.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Public transit workers are protected by assault-and-battery statute.
Statute number(s): Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 265, section 13D, as amended by 2025 Mass. Acts ch. 79
Covered worker/setting: Public transit worker, including operators and other covered transit employees
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault and battery on a public employee provision covers public transit workers performing duties, including offensive physical contact and bodily-fluid/substance forms.
Punishment / grading: Not less than 90 days nor more than 2.5 years in house of correction, or fine $500 to $5,000, or both.
Notes: 2025 act broadened and updated the transit-worker coverage.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No current public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Statute number(s): MCL sections 750.81, 750.81a, 750.82; public-utility worker provisions sections 750.81e-750.81g do not cover transit operators
Covered worker/setting: General assault/battery victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault/battery statutes apply; separate public-utility-worker assault statutes are for electric/gas/water/telecom/cable-type utility workers, not public transit operators.
Punishment / grading: Basic assault/battery misdemeanor up to 93 days/$500; aggravated assault misdemeanor up to 1 year/$1,000; felonious assault felony up to 4 years/$2,000.
Notes: Recent transit-worker assault bills existed, but no enacted current MCL transit-operator provision was located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Separate assault/bodily-fluid offense for transit operators, plus transit-operator interference.
Covered worker/setting: Transit operator; operator of transit vehicle; light rail, special transportation, commuter rail contexts
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 609.2231 subd. 11 covers assaulting a transit operator or intentionally throwing/transferring bodily fluids onto the operator while the operator is performing duties in/near a transit vehicle. section 609.855 covers intentionally interfering with or obstructing transit-vehicle operation, with higher penalty if force, violence, or threat is used.
Felony or misdemeanor: Gross misdemeanor; felony-level penalty for force/threat interference
Punishment / grading: Transit-operator assault/bodily-fluid offense: gross misdemeanor, up to 364 days/$3,000. Interference with force/violence/threat: up to 3 years/$5,000; otherwise up to 90 days/$1,000.
Notes: Strong transit-specific coverage.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Limited school-bus-specific protection; no public-transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: School bus driver; general assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Simple assault and aggravated assault penalties are enhanced when committed against a school bus driver acting within the scope of duty, among other listed protected persons.
Felony or misdemeanor: Felony for protected school-bus-driver assault forms
Punishment / grading: Simple assault on listed school bus driver: up to 5 years/$1,000. Aggravated assault on listed school bus driver: up to 30 years/$5,000.
Notes: No state public-transit bus-operator assault provision located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Mass transit workers can be special victims; bus hijacking statute also protects bus drivers/attendants/guards.
Covered worker/setting: Mass transit worker; bus driver, attendant, or guard
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault statutes grade offenses more severely when the victim is a special victim, which includes a mass transit worker. Bus hijacking statute covers assaulting, threatening, intimidating, or battering a bus driver/attendant/guard to interfere with duties or gain control of a bus.
Punishment / grading: Assault grades increase for special victims; assault 2 can be Class B felony in special-victim cases. Bus hijacking is Class B felony; assault with intent to commit bus hijacking is Class C felony, or Class A felony with dangerous/deadly weapon.
Notes: Missouri has both general assault special-victim coverage and a bus-hijacking-specific law.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault and aggravated assault statutes apply to injuries, reasonable apprehension of bodily injury, physical contact, serious bodily injury, or weapon scenarios.
Punishment / grading: Assault generally misdemeanor; felony forms apply for aggravated assault, weapon, serious bodily injury, and protected victim categories not including transit drivers.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault degrees cover serious bodily injury, bodily injury with a dangerous instrument, bodily injury, or threatened bodily injury.
Punishment / grading: First degree Class II felony; second degree Class IIA felony; third degree Class I misdemeanor or Class IIIA felony when committed in menacing manner.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver assault category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault and battery statutes specifically cover transit operators.
Covered worker/setting: Transit operator
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault/battery committed against a transit operator triggers enhanced classifications; deadly weapon and substantial bodily harm produce felony treatment.
Punishment / grading: Assault on transit operator: gross misdemeanor; with deadly weapon/present ability: category B felony, 1 to 6 years and possible fine up to $5,000. Battery on transit operator: gross misdemeanor; substantial bodily harm or deadly weapon: category B felony, 2 to 10 years and possible fine up to $10,000.
Notes: Strong transit-operator-specific coverage.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General first-degree, second-degree, and simple assault statutes apply based on injury, weapon, intent, and recklessness.
Punishment / grading: First-degree assault Class A felony; second-degree assault generally Class B felony; simple assault misdemeanor or violation depending facts.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver assault category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault on bus, rail, and school-bus personnel is elevated.
Covered worker/setting: Operator of a motorbus, employee of a rail passenger service, school bus driver, and related transit personnel while performing duties
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Simple assault becomes aggravated assault when committed against listed transit/school-bus personnel; if bodily injury occurs it is third degree, otherwise fourth degree.
Punishment / grading: Third degree: 3 to 5 years, fine up to $15,000. Fourth degree: up to 18 months, fine up to $10,000.
Notes: Includes public bus and rail personnel and school bus drivers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes for bus hijacking/assault with intent to commit bus hijacking; no ordinary transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: Bus driver, attendant, or guard; bus passengers
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Bus hijacking covers seizing or exercising control of a bus by force, violence, threat, or intimidation. Assault with intent to commit bus hijacking includes assault, threat, intimidation, or violence toward a bus driver/attendant/guard to interfere with duties or toward passengers to gain control of a bus.
Punishment / grading: Bus hijacking: third-degree felony. Assault with intent to commit bus hijacking: fourth-degree felony. General penalties: third-degree felony commonly 3 years; fourth-degree felony 18 months, subject to New Mexico sentencing rules.
Notes: Focuses on control/interference with bus operation, not all assaults on drivers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault on transit workers is assault in the second degree.
Covered worker/setting: Train operator, ticket inspector, conductor, signalperson, bus operator, station agent, station cleaner, terminal cleaner, and related transit workers
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault 2 includes causing physical injury to specified transit workers with intent to prevent them from performing lawful duties.
Punishment / grading: Class D violent felony; determinate sentence commonly 2 to 7 years depending offender history and sentencing rules.
Notes: New York has detailed enumerated transit-worker categories.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault on a public transit operator is specifically covered.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit operator, including public/private contractor employees performing transit-operator duties
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault or assault and battery on a public transit operator while the operator is discharging or attempting to discharge official duties.
Punishment / grading: Class A1 misdemeanor; maximum punishment up to 150 days depending prior record and sentencing level.
Notes: Covers operators employed by private contracting agencies as well as public agencies.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General assault and aggravated assault statutes apply based on bodily injury, serious bodily injury, dangerous weapon, and culpability.
Punishment / grading: Simple assault generally Class A misdemeanor, with felony grading for protected victims/serious factors; aggravated assault Class C felony.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Limited school-bus-specific protection; no public-transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Statute number(s): Ohio Rev. Code section 2903.13; general felonious/aggravated assault sections 2903.11, 2903.12
Covered worker/setting: School bus driver, operator, or monitor; general assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault statute includes enhanced treatment when the victim is a school bus driver, operator, or monitor and the offense occurs while performing duties, during boarding/exiting, or in the immediate vicinity of a school bus.
Felony or misdemeanor: Fifth-degree felony for school-bus-driver assault; general offenses vary
Punishment / grading: Fifth-degree felony generally 6 to 12 months and possible fine up to $2,500.
Notes: No public-transit bus-operator enhancement located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes for bus hijacking/assault with intent to commit bus hijacking; no ordinary transit-driver assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: Bus driver, attendant, or guard; bus passengers
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Bus hijacking and assault with intent to commit bus hijacking cover force, violence, threat, intimidation, or assault toward the driver/attendant/guard to interfere with duties or gain control of a bus.
Punishment / grading: Bus hijacking: felony with imprisonment up to 20 years and/or fine up to $20,000. Assault with intent to commit bus hijacking: felony up to 10 years and/or fine up to $5,000; higher if dangerous/deadly weapon applies.
Notes: Focuses on control/interference with bus operation.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault on public transit vehicle operator is assault in the third degree.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit vehicle operator while operating or in control of a vehicle
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault in the third degree includes causing physical injury to the operator of a public transit vehicle while the operator is in control of or operating the vehicle.
Punishment / grading: Class C felony: up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to $125,000.
Notes: Official Oregon text can also be checked through the Oregon Legislature ORS pages.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Public transportation employees are protected under aggravated assault.
Covered worker/setting: Public transportation employee
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Aggravated assault includes attempts to cause, or intentionally/knowingly/recklessly causing, bodily injury or serious bodily injury to listed protected persons, including public transportation employees, while in performance of duty.
Felony or misdemeanor: Felony of the first or second degree depending injury/paragraph
Punishment / grading: Serious bodily injury form: felony of the first degree, max 20 years/$25,000. Bodily injury form: felony of the second degree, max 10 years/$25,000.
Notes: Use exact subsection based on injury level and protected-employee category.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Rhode Island Public Transit Authority bus drivers are listed in assault-on-public-officials statute.
Covered worker/setting: RIPTA bus driver and other listed public officials/employees
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault or battery upon listed public officials/employees includes Rhode Island Public Transit Authority bus drivers.
Punishment / grading: Felony punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to $1,500.
Notes: Transit coverage is specifically tied to RIPTA bus drivers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes for interference with public transportation operators/vehicles; school-bus protections also exist.
Covered worker/setting: Public transportation vehicle operator; school bus driver/personnel
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 58-23-1830 prohibits obstructing, hindering, interfering with, disrupting, or disturbing the operation or operator of a public transportation vehicle. Separate school-bus laws prohibit interference/threats and student assault/battery against school personnel including bus drivers.
Felony or misdemeanor: Misdemeanor for public-transportation interference and school-bus interference
Punishment / grading: Public transportation interference: first offense up to 30 days/$200; second up to 60 days/$500; third/subsequent up to 90 days/$1,000. Student assault/battery on school personnel: misdemeanor up to 1 year/$1,000.
Notes: No separate felony assault enhancement for public transit operators located, but interference law is transit-specific.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General simple assault and aggravated assault statutes apply based on attempts, injury, fear, serious bodily injury, and weapon/dangerous-substance factors.
Punishment / grading: Simple assault generally Class 1 misdemeanor; aggravated assault generally Class 3 felony.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No current public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located; historical transit-employee aggravated-assault language appears to have been deleted.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Current assault/aggravated-assault statutes apply based on bodily injury, fear, offensive contact, serious injury, deadly weapon, strangulation, and other general factors.
Punishment / grading: Assault generally Class A or B misdemeanor depending conduct; aggravated assault generally Class C or D felony depending facts.
Distinct from violence in general?: No current distinct transit category located
Notes: Older compilations list a transportation-system employee provision under section 39-13-102; current accessible text does not show that transit-specific language.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Partial. Public transit drivers employed by a governmental transit agency may be protected as public servants, but there is no bus-driver-specific category.
Covered worker/setting: Public servant while lawfully discharging official duty; general assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault causing bodily injury to a person the actor knows is a public servant lawfully discharging duty is elevated. This can cover publicly employed transit workers, but not because of bus-driver status itself.
Punishment / grading: Bodily-injury assault on public servant: third-degree felony, 2 to 10 years and possible fine up to $10,000. General assault otherwise ranges from Class C/A misdemeanor to felony; aggravated assault can be second- or first-degree felony.
Distinct from violence in general?: Partly; public-servant status, not transit-driver status
Notes: Private or contractor transit operators may not fit the public-servant enhancement; check employment/status facts.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes for bus hijacking and assault with intent to commit bus hijacking; other bus-conduct rules also exist.
Statute number(s): Utah Code sections 76-9-1502, 76-9-1503; formerly sections 76-10-1504 et seq.
Covered worker/setting: Bus driver, attendant, or guard; bus passengers
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Bus hijacking covers seizing or exercising control of a bus by force, violence, threat, or intimidation. Assault with intent to commit bus hijacking covers assault/threat/intimidation/battery on a bus driver/attendant/guard to interfere with duties or gain control of a bus.
Punishment / grading: Bus hijacking: first-degree felony, generally 5 years to life. Assault with intent to commit bus hijacking: second-degree felony, generally 1 to 15 years; first-degree felony if dangerous weapon/firearm used.
Notes: Renumbered in 2025 from Title 76, Chapter 10, Part 15 to Title 76, Chapter 9, Part 15.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: No public-transit-driver-specific assault enhancement located.
Covered worker/setting: General assault victims
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: General simple assault and aggravated assault statutes apply based on attempts, injury, weapon, serious injury, and protected categories not including transit drivers.
Punishment / grading: Simple assault generally up to 1 year/$1,000; aggravated assault generally up to 15 years/$10,000 depending subsection.
Notes: No current state public-transit/bus-driver assault category located.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault/battery on a public transportation vehicle operator has an additional transit ban.
Covered worker/setting: Operator of a vehicle operated by a public transportation service
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault or assault and battery against a person known or having reason to know is an operator of a vehicle operated by a public transportation service and engaged in official duties.
Punishment / grading: Class 1 misdemeanor: up to 12 months/$2,500; sentence also must prohibit entering or riding in any vehicle operated by that public transportation service for at least 6 months.
Notes: Transit-specific sanction is mandatory ridership/entry ban.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Transit operator/driver assault is assault in the third degree; separate unlawful-transit-conduct misdemeanor also exists.
Covered worker/setting: Transit operator/driver, immediate supervisor, mechanic, or security officer employed by transit company/provider; school bus driver and staff also listed
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Assault in the third degree includes assaulting a transit operator/driver or listed transit employee while performing official duties; separate statute prohibits unlawful transit conduct that interferes with public transportation.
Felony or misdemeanor: Class C felony for assault 3; misdemeanor for unlawful transit conduct
Punishment / grading: Class C felony: up to 5 years/$10,000. Unlawful transit conduct: misdemeanor.
Notes: Washington explicitly includes public and private transit company employees and contracted providers.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Assault/battery/malicious or unlawful assault on person in charge of public conveyance is separately punished.
Covered worker/setting: Driver, conductor, motorman, captain, pilot, or other person in charge of vehicle/boat used for public conveyance, acting in official capacity
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: Statute covers malicious assault, unlawful assault, battery, and assault upon the operator/person in charge of a public conveyance while acting in official capacity.
Punishment / grading: Malicious assault: felony 3 to 15 years. Unlawful assault: felony 2 to 5 years. Battery: misdemeanor 1 to 12 months/$500, with repeat felonies. Assault: misdemeanor 24 hours to 6 months and/or fine up to $200.
Notes: Covers public-conveyance operators broadly, not just buses.

Transit/bus-driver-specific treatment: Yes. Battery to a public transit vehicle operator/driver/passenger is a felony.
Covered worker/setting: Public transit vehicle operator, driver, or passenger
Statutory language / trigger (condensed: section 940.62(1)(e) covers battery causing bodily harm to a public transit vehicle operator, driver, or passenger while the victim is in/on the public transit vehicle, after being forced/directed to leave, or while offender prevents/attempts to prevent access.
Punishment / grading: Class I felony: up to 3 years 6 months imprisonment and/or $10,000 fine.
Notes: Current law reorganized this coverage in 2025; older sources may cite section 940.20.
